summary: Octagonal brick light on Chambers Island in Green Bay, first lit in 1868; automated in 1955, replaced by a skeletal tower in 1961, and a town park since 1976.

structures.note: Tower of cream-colored Milwaukee brick, built into the dwelling (NRHP; LighthouseFriends). Lantern removed 1958. Height 44 ft 9 in to the ventilator ball (LighthouseFriends).
One-and-a-half-story brick dwelling and kitchen (LighthouseFriends; NRHP).
97-foot skeletal tower near the oil house, erected 1961 (LighthouseFriends); the parcel under it was not deeded to the town in 1976.

access.note: Town of Gibraltar park. Grounds open; dwelling and tower closed. Public dock; lighthouse 1.5 miles from the dock; tours when a volunteer is on site.

events.note: G. J. Pendergrast reports to the Board of Navy Commissioners that the island lies in the track of vessels (LighthouseFriends quoting the report).
Congress appropriates $25,000 for the Chambers Island light, Fox River range lights and a Peshtigo Reef beacon (LighthouseFriends).
Crew from Detroit lands June 1868; dwelling and tower built of Milwaukee brick.
Lewis S. Williams makes the first lighting, 1 October 1868.
Flash interval cut from one minute to thirty seconds; the report dates it 15 July 1899, but its list of changes gives 13 July.
Fourth-order Fresnel lens (made 1892 by F. Barbier & Cie.) substituted (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper Rollefson and assistant Ledwell aid three sailors whose motor boat burned and take them to Marinette (fiscal 1916 record of assistance, page image read; LighthouseFriends).
Lighthouse Service Bulletin lists the station among lights changed from oil to incandescent oil vapor.
Keepers reach the station across seven miles of ice on skis after a report that the acetylene winter light was not burning.
Marker radiobeacon established on the island.
Coast Guard automates the light and removes the landing pier and boatways.
Lantern room removed from the tower; LighthouseFriends reports the lens was sold at a surplus auction.
Coast Guard erects a 97-foot skeletal tower near the oil house, replacing the historic tower's light.
National Register nomination prepared 1975; the station is listed on the Register (Town of Gibraltar page).
Land (except the skeletal tower parcel) deeded to the Town of Gibraltar for park purposes, 10 March 1976.
Park opens the year after the deed.

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends gives a focal plane of 68 feet (20.7 m); the USLHS record gives 20.73 m. The record's 29.6 m matches the Wikidata figure of 30 m only.
The NRHP nomination describes a three-story octagonal tower built into the dwelling, and LighthouseFriends describes a square base with an octagonal upper part. Neither describes a conical tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 1961 (Wikidata) and 1868 (USLHS). The 1868 date is the first lighting (LighthouseFriends, USLHS, NRHP 'erected in 1868'); 1961 is the year the historic tower's light was replaced by the skeletal tower.
Record's 29.6 m (Wikidata) against 20.7 m (LighthouseFriends, 68 ft; USLHS 20.73 m). The NRHP gives the focal plane as 'approximately 638 feet M.S.L.', on a different base.
LighthouseFriends describes the dwellings as cream-colored Milwaukee brick; the NRHP nomination calls the Chambers brick buff-colored. Both are stated in the story.

notes_for_editor: CHECKED 2026-10-22. Quotes: 76 found on the first run. (1) The 1916 rescue (Rollefson and Ledwell, three shipwrecked sailors, motor boat destroyed by fire, taken to Marinette) is now corroborated by the fiscal 1916 Commissioner record of assistance: the page image (scan p.170, printed p.61) reads 'J. J. Rollefson, keeper; E. R. Ledwell, assistant keeper, Chambers Island Light Station, Wis.' beside 'Motor boat Starlight, Marinette, Wis.' and 'Gave food and clothing to 3 shipwrecked sailors whose motor boat was destroyed by fire, and took men over to Marinette, Wis.' The page is a rescue table, not a personnel list; the footnote is relabelled. The OCR of the names is matched to the roster by station and period (roster 1906-1925 for Rollefson; Ledwell assistant 1913-1925), and the image confirms the names in the same row. (2) Tower height: LighthouseFriends 44 ft 9 in (13.6 m) to the ventilator ball; record 20.0 m. Not corrected here; flagged. The record's 'Wikipedia lead' reference is not cited in the story. (3) Tower shape: LighthouseFriends square base with octagonal top; NRHP three-story octagonal tower in the NE corner. Both stated. (4) Focal plane: NRHP 'approximately 638 feet M.S.L.' vs LighthouseFriends 68 feet; the story says they are not reconciled. (5) 1899 characteristic change: 1900 Board report text says 15 July 1899; the same report's list of changes says 13 July; LighthouseFriends 15 July. Both stated. Fiscal-year labels: the 1899 shipment and the 1900 report are both fiscal-year reports (July to June), consistent with a change on 15 July 1899. (6) The 1866 appropriation, the Pendergrast 1837 report, the Williams deed, and the 1875 ice and strawberry anecdotes are LighthouseFriends accounts, not checked against statutes or the 1868 Board report (not in the corpus). (7) 1931 Bulletin: the February 1931 'skiis' passage is on PDF p.6 (checked); the index entry 'skiis needed to reach Chambers Island' is on PDF p.4, page 56 (checked). The story says 'in the winter of 1931' rather than February (the month comes from LighthouseFriends). (8) Brick colour: LighthouseFriends cream-colored; NRHP buff-colored. Stated in the story. (9) The station record's status 'inactive' sits oddly with the NRHP's 'a fully automated light continues this service'; the historic tower went dark in 1961 and the skeletal tower carries the light. Not changed. (10) Privacy: the adjacent owner who leased the lighthouse (named in the NRHP nomination) is not named; the lens buyer and the post-1976 caretakers (LighthouseFriends names Joel and Mary Blahnik) are not named. (11) Wikipedia consulted as a lead only; not cited. The Hello Door County blog (2024) is not cited. (12) Fiscal-year fixes applied: 1893, 1896-97, 1899 and 1900 reports are now labelled as fiscal years.
